newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban rebels said to have entered Afghan capital.
newsitem.headline: Taleban rebels said to have entered Afghan capital.

text.p: Afghanistan's rebel Taleban Islamic militia have entered the eastern part of the capital Kabul and are fighting government forces there, a Taleban source in Pakistan said on Thursday.

The source, who did not want to be identified, said the rebels entered the city area overnight and were only about five km (three miles) from the presidential palace. There was no immediate independent confirmation of the report.
The Taleban source in the northwestern Pakistani town of Peshawar denied a Kabul government report on Wednesday night that its forces had repulsed the militia assault from the east of the capital.
He said the Taleban entered the city area from Pul-i-Charkhi village, which was captured on Wednesday.
